_comment: MOH-wide O3 runtime configuration. Loaded after config-core.json and before the
programme and site layers, so it overrides core and is overridden by site.
Must be listed in SPA_CONFIG_URLS — see IMPLEMENTATION.md §7.
_comment_service_queues: concepts MUST be set. Every key below has a built-in default in
esm-service-queues-app pointing at a RefApp demo concept that does not exist in this
database, and the app sends those UUIDs straight to the backend — queue-entry?status=
<uuid> then answers 500 'Unable to find concept' and the dashboard renders an error.
Leaving the block empty is NOT the same as leaving it unset: the defaults still apply.

@openmrs/esm-service-queues-app._comment_serve_redirect: LE-121. Serve target per service (patch-service-queues-serve-redirect.cjs). Unmapped services open the chart.

@openmrs/esm-appointments-app._comment_display: Appointments is a module-access entitlement. Read is View Appointments and View Appointment Services. Write adds Manage Appointments (appointments-api 2.1.0). getAllAppointments, search, and get-by-uuid accept View Appointments. getAllAppointmentServices, used by GET /appointment/appointmentSummary and GET /appointmentService/all/default, accepts View Appointment Services. The home link is the extension clinical-appointments-dashboard-link; this module display condition applies to that extension. The framework privilege check still shows the extension to System Developer. Direct URL access is unchanged.

_comment_home_dashboards: LE-395. /home opens the dashboard defaultDashboardPerRole names for one of the user's roles,
else 'service-queues', else the first dashboard left in homepage-dashboard-slot. Each
dashboard below is shown only to a user holding EVERY privilege its data needs, so no role
lands on, or sees a link to, a dashboard that can only answer 403.
LE-397. The national roles land on their own app's dashboard, which the app registers in
homepage-dashboard-slot gated by the same privilege as its page (routes.json): audit-log
(View Audit Log), indicator-reports (Export National Report), sync-status (View Sync Status),
sync-conflicts (Resolve Sync Conflicts). A name whose dashboard is missing (an app build
older than LE-397) falls back to the first dashboard left, as before. A user with several
mapped roles lands on the first of them in the session's role order.

@openmrs/esm-home-app._comment_display: homepage-dashboard-slot belongs to esm-home-app. Display conditions are set on that slot's configure entry, the same way add-patient-action is gated. patient-lists-dashboard-link is the Patient Lists card; it loads GET /cohortm/cohort, which cohort 3.7.3 authorizes with View Cohorts In Cohort Module. ward-dashboard-link is the Wards card; GET /admissionLocation/{uuid} is BedManagementService.getAdmissionLocationByLocation, authorized by Get Admission Locations or Get Beds (bedmanagement 7.2.0, requireAll false). The card requires Get Admission Locations. These are not module-level Display conditions on esm-patient-list-management-app or esm-ward-app, because a partial module config for those apps crashes the home shell. Direct URL access is unchanged. System Developer still sees both cards.

_comment_app_menu: LE-397. The RefApp's app menu entries carry no privilege of their own, so every signed-in user
saw them, the national roles included. Each is shown only to a user holding what its page
needs: System Administration the legacy admin's View Administration Functions, the queue
screen the same queue privileges as the service queues dashboard, Dispensing Get Medication
Dispense (the Pharmacist). LiberiaEMR's own entries are gated in their routes.json.

_comment: DAK 3.1 patient card. Registration opens the chart; the banner's Actions > Print identifier
sticker prints the card. Its layout and logo are in the backend

_comment_patient_banner: Contact Details in the patient banner lists these attributes. Text formats only: the banner
renders the raw value, and a coded attribute's value is an object. Telephone is the app default.

_comment_idle_timeout: Minutes of human inactivity for the login-app watcher. Maven filtering leaves this as a string such as "10".
This is not logoutIdleTimeoutMinutes. See docs/security/moh-ict-sop-mapping.md.

_comment_reports: MOH indicator report runner (LE-335). reportUuids is the list offered, in this order;
a report left out is not shown. Set here, not in config-central.json: central loads this
layer too, and the app reads its facility or central role from the reports module at
runtime. mflCodeAttributeTypeUuid lets the central picker find a facility by MFL code.

_comment_immunization_entry: Immunizations Add uses this widget, which opens the national Immunization form in
patient-form-entry-workspace. The upstream immunization-details-widget is removed
from the immunizations dashboard so it no longer opens the FHIR immunization workspace.
formUuids keeps the table on Immunization encounters. FHIR history stays on the
read-only immunizations history card and on Previous immunizations.
_comment_routine_immunizations: One routineImmunizations object feeds the routine schedule and dose sequencing.
Schedule policy and sequence rules stay in the ESM. UUID metadata is runtime config.
vaccineConceptUuids is an object: a site can replace one dose key and the other national values remain.
nationalFormUuids and ancFormUuids are arrays. Frontend config replaces an array wholesale,
so a site that sets either key must list every form version it still wants counted.
var.form.immunization.uuid stays the current form. The v1-* variables are frozen historical identities.
v1.13 is current. v1.12 stays in this list so encounters saved on it still count.
The current variable is also in the list so the next version bump stays visible until it is frozen.
fhirDoseMappings stays empty until a deployment supplies verified generic vaccine codings.
Configured doses with no sequence rule are recognized and do not block other series.
ancTtConceptUuids maps canonical TD dose IDs to ANC Date-of-TT concepts. TD1 uses the unsuffixed TD concept.
